name: Pragma TacWeave Ballistic Underlayer
description: Slim-cut, body-conforming underlayer in matte slate with subtle hexagonal weave texture barely visible at the collar and cuffs. From outside, it reads as an athletic undershirt. Inside, six overlapping panels of soft ballistic weave — shear-thickening fluid suspended in para-aramid matrix — cover the torso and upper back. The fabric breathes adequately, sits flat under dress shirts or jackets without visible bulk, and resists printing against the skin. Gene-channel vents along the lower back accommodate tail-base modifications.
functionality: NIJ Level II soft ballistic protection across torso panels; passes as athletic underlayer in most visual inspection contexts; gene-vent rear panels for tail-base geneware; moisture management for all-day desk or field wear.
what_it_says: You've thought about what happens when things go wrong, and you've done something about it without making it anyone's business.
worn_by: small business owners in contested districts
story_hooks: A Tier 3 accountant starts wearing one after their firm's senior partner gets shot in the lobby — nobody at the office knows.
A recovered round embedded in the ballistic panel is the wrong caliber for any licensed weapon in this district.
The gene-vent panel has been retrofitted with a hidden pocket — slim, flat, body-temperature — currently holding a data chip.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively simple athletic underlayer with a sleek, form-fitting silhouette that conceals its tactical purpose. From the outside, it appears as a premium performance base layer — understated and professional enough to wear beneath corpo dress shirts without raising suspicion. The matte slate finish has a subtle luster that catches light without sheen.
physical_description.fit: Slim-cut and body-conforming, engineered to compress against the torso without visible bulk under outerwear. The fit is snug but not restrictive, designed to maximize protection panel coverage while maintaining freedom of movement. Minimal print-through when worn under fitted garments.
physical_description.primary_material: Para-aramid matrix with shear-thickening fluid suspension in inner panels; outer layer is breathable synth-blend athletic knit
physical_description.texture: Matte, almost velvety outer surface with barely perceptible hexagonal weave pattern visible only at collar and cuff edges. Inner panels have a slightly tacky, dampening quality when touched directly — the signature feel of active ballistic weave
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte slate gray throughout with black micro-ribbing at collar, cuffs, and hem. No visible branding on exterior surface
physical_description.closures: Seamless friction-fit construction; crew neck with reinforced binding; short sleeves with elastic cuff
distinctive_features: Six overlapping ballistic weave panels across torso and upper back — invisible from outside
Shear-thickening fluid suspension hardens on impact, disperses kinetic energy
Gene-channel vents along lower back for tail-base and spinal-column augmentations
Flat-lock seams throughout to prevent snagging on internal tech or modifications
Moisture-wicking inner surface designed to interface with subcutaneous cooling implants
Pragma Systems discreet label at back neckline only
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional — accessible to working-class security, medical responders, and field operatives, but represents genuine ballistic-grade protection rather than cosmetic styling
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corporate security personnel, field medics, independent fixers, and anyone who needs protection but can't advertise it. Signals 'I've thought about survival' without screaming 'tactical gear.' Popular in the GLMZ among those navigating volatile sectors.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn when new; develops subtle creasing at articulation points (shoulders, elbows, lower back) with regular use. The matte finish hides dust and minor staining well. Ballistic panels degrade slowly — noticeable loss of shear-thickening response after 18-24 months of regular defensive use
